scientific_question: Can the official StructMem runtime dependencies be resolved twice into one byte-identical Linux x86_64 Python 3.11 uv lock under exclusive PyPI and PyTorch CPU routes?
decision_informed: Whether a hash-complete, route-separated, project-owned offline wheelhouse can be frozen for StructMem without modifying a shared environment.
scientific_evidence_role: dependency-resolution evidence only; no wheel acquisition, installation, model import, lifecycle, numerical result, superiority, or SOTA claim

prospective_specialization.rank_bm25: Freeze rank-bm25==0.2.2, the upstream lower bound, before any import or result is observed.
prospective_specialization.torch: Preserve upstream torch==2.8.0 semantics while exclusively routing its Linux wheel to the official PyTorch CPU index because StructMem's LLMLingua component is CPU-bound in the frozen lifecycle.
prospective_specialization.optional_groups: Exclude llms, mcp, fluxmem, and dev groups because the frozen adapter uses the OpenAI-compatible manager, OpenAI-compatible embedder, Qdrant local mode, and LLMLingua-2 only.
prospective_specialization.deduplication: Represent the duplicated upstream httpx==0.28.1 declaration once without changing its constraint.

toolchain.shared_prefix_access: read-only interpreter selection; no package is installed into its prefix

resource_gate.start_condition: Wave1 controller is independently TERMINAL_ACCEPTED, all Wave1 services and evaluators have stopped, and no process references either fresh output root.
resource_gate.why: The stage performs repeated online dependency resolution and must not perturb the active numerical comparison workload.

acceptance: All source, workspace, uv, and Python identities match their frozen bytes and hashes.
The workspace contains exactly 58 unique exact-pinned direct dependencies and routes Torch exclusively to the official CPU index.
Both fresh uv lock passes complete under Python 3.11 with zero retries, no cache, one concurrent download, and no Python download.
The two uv.lock outputs are non-empty and byte-identical.
No dependency or model is installed or loaded, and the shared Python prefix is unchanged.
The evidence root is TERMINAL_ACCEPTED without TERMINAL_REJECTED and all evidence files have retained SHA-256 values.
failure: Any premature start, collision, identity mismatch, dependency conflict, registry error, network error, timeout, lock disagreement, implicit Python acquisition, or evidence mismatch seals the fresh evidence root as TERMINAL_REJECTED and retains both partial workspaces.
next_gate_after_acceptance: Independently audit and archive the canonical lock, export a hash-complete route-separated requirements set, then freeze an offline wheelhouse. Lock acceptance does not authorize wheel download, installation, model import, lifecycle, or numerical execution.
prohibited_actions: starting before Wave1 terminal acceptance and complete service release
changing an upstream exact dependency after observing import or benchmark outcomes
routing Torch through an implicit mirror or the default PyPI index
using retries, cache, concurrent resolution, a different uv/Python, or Python auto-download
installing into or modifying the shared Python 3.11 environment
deleting or repairing a rejected output root in place
populating a comparison-table numeric cell from dependency resolution
